Confirmed: no `tsconfig.json` exists at all, even though `package.json` references one for `build` and `typecheck`. That's a real gap worth flagging too. I now have everything needed.

## Findings, most to least severe

**1. The actual bug: hand-editing a generated file, with no guardrail stopping it.**
`src/db/generated-types.ts:1` is headed `// AUTO-GENERATED. Do not edit.`, and `CLAUDE.md:28` says "Never commit generated files by hand" — but the session edited it directly anyway to add `currency`. The real source of truth, `src/db/schema.ts`, still has no `currency` field on `refunds` (it's only on `orders`). So the first time anyone/CI ran `pnpm db:generate`, it silently overwrote the hand-added field — that's the "currency field disappeared" report and almost certainly the red CI (`orderRepo.ts` referencing a field that regeneration wiped out).
- **Change `CLAUDE.md`**: add a concrete "Database schema changes" section: edit `src/db/schema.ts` first, then run `pnpm db:generate`; never touch `src/db/generated-types.ts` by hand. The current rule is too generic to connect to this specific file.
- **Change `.github/workflows/ci.yml`**: add a drift check — run `pnpm db:generate` then `git diff --exit-code` — so a hand-edited/out-of-sync generated file fails CI instead of silently reverting on the next regeneration.

**2. `CLAUDE.md:36` tells the agent to run `pnpm test:unit`, but that script doesn't exist.**
`package.json` only defines `test`. The session hit `ERR_PNPM_NO_SCRIPT` and had to guess the right command. This is a stale instruction that will fail identically every session.
- **Change `CLAUDE.md`**: line 36, `pnpm test:unit` → `pnpm test` (matching what CI and package.json actually use).

**3. An explicit architecture rule was broken and nothing catches it mechanically.**
`src/core/router.ts:2` imports `query` straight from `src/internal/pg-driver.ts`, violating `CLAUDE.md:15` ("Never import from `src/internal/*` outside the module that owns it") and `docs/architecture/request-flow.md:8` ("Handlers never touch the database driver directly"). It's still in the file — the reviewer agent didn't catch it either, because it reviewed only against `CODING_STANDARDS.md` (`CODING_STANDARDS.md:3`: "Read during review, not during implementation"), which doesn't mention import boundaries or `any` at all. Rules that only live in prose in `CLAUDE.md` aren't being checked at review time.
- **Change `CODING_STANDARDS.md`**: add a line telling review to also check the diff against `CLAUDE.md`'s Rules section (import boundaries, no `any`, `Result<T,E>`) — right now that file implicitly claims to be the complete review checklist and isn't.
- **Change `eslint.config.js`**: add an import-boundary rule (e.g. `no-restricted-imports`/`eslint-plugin-boundaries`) blocking `src/internal/*` from anywhere outside `src/db`, so this is enforced by tooling instead of by an agent remembering a prose rule.

**4. CI doesn't run lint, and lint wouldn't catch the `any` violation anyway.**
`.github/workflows/ci.yml` only runs `typecheck` and `test` — `pnpm lint` is never invoked. Separately, `eslint.config.js` only extends `js.configs.recommended`; there's no `@typescript-eslint` plugin, so `no-explicit-any` isn't enforced even if lint ran. `CLAUDE.md:14` ("Never use `any`") is currently unenforced prose — the session added an `any`-returning `findRefund` specifically because narrowing "looked like a bigger change."
- **Change `.github/workflows/ci.yml`**: add a `pnpm lint` step.
- **Change `eslint.config.js`**: add `@typescript-eslint` with `no-explicit-any: "error"`.

**5. There is no `tsconfig.json` at all**, despite `package.json` referencing one for both `build` (`tsc -p tsconfig.json`) and `typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit`). Without it, type-checking runs on default (non-strict) compiler options, so even legitimate type safety (e.g. catching implicit `any`, missing fields after the generated-types edit) is weaker than the rules in `CLAUDE.md` assume.
- **Add `tsconfig.json`** with at least `strict: true`, so `pnpm typecheck` actually backs up the "never use `any`" / type-safety rules instead of running on defaults.

**6. `pnpm dev` is unusable for the verification step `CLAUDE.md` and your own process expect.**
`package.json:5`: `"dev": "tsx watch src/cli/serve.ts > /dev/null 2>&1"` redirects all output (including errors) to `/dev/null`. The session tried to start the dev server to confirm the endpoint worked and "never saw a log line or an error" — the script itself guarantees that outcome.
- **Change `package.json`**: drop the `> /dev/null 2>&1` redirection from the `dev` script (or add a separate quiet variant if the silence is intentional for some other consumer).

**7. The mandatory pre-task step is pure noise for most tasks.**
`CLAUDE.md:7-8` unconditionally requires `pnpm status-report` "before starting any task." That script (`package.json:11`) just `cat`s `docs/status-dump.txt`, a 422-line generic per-module status dump with no relevance to a refunds/currency change — the session itself noted "nothing in it was relevant." This burns context and a tool call on every single task regardless of fit.
- **Change `CLAUDE.md`**: either drop this requirement or scope it ("only when working on deployment/ops issues"), and/or make `docs/status-dump.txt` targeted/searchable rather than a full unconditional dump.
